title: UniPoolerV2 constructor validates only the pair's token set, not pair_ == router.factory().getPair(sUSDS, phUSD); combined with a permissionless, possibly-empty factory pair, the cutover can be decoupled (non-canonical pair) or permanently griefed (dust pre-seed at an arbitrary ratio, MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY lock)
description: pool()/quotePool size s and read reserves from _pair while router executes on factory pair: mis-sized s, wrong quote, LP minted is a different token than pair() reports (rescuable). Floors bound loss.
impact: If deployed with a token-matching pair from a different factory, pool()/quotePool size from _pair while the router executes on the factory pair: mis-sized zaps bounded by floors; LP lands as a different token (rescuable).
attackPath: Owner-supplied constructor argument only; no third-party path
assumptions: Deploy script passes a non-canonical pair
severityJustification: Missing deploy-time validation (require(factory.getPair(sUSDS, phUSD) == pair_)). Supplying the wrong pair address is an obvious-consequence misconfiguration (story-faithfulness already suppressed it under Law 3), floors bound any loss, and LP is rescuable. QA hardening.
recommendation: constructor require(factory.getPair(sUSDS, phUSD) == pair_) or cutover-script assertion
knownIssueCheck: No KI match. KI#4 (owner trust) does not cover facet B: the dust pre-seed grief is a THIRD-PARTY action on a permissionless factory pair; facet A (non-canonical pair accepted) is a non-obvious deploy footgun.
ledgerMatch: None. Q-01 98c9fc4523 (fixed, zero-address ctor validation) is a different root cause.
fingerprintNote: Facet A keeps the consolidated fingerprint (its root cause IS pair-not-bound-to-router-factory).
